newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan ruling party in Australia investment - paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan ruling party in Australia investment - paper.

text.p: TAIPEI, Oct 27 (Ruter) - Taiwan's ruling Nationalist Party has recently obtained approval from the Australian government to purchase 4,000 hectares of land there for its aquatic breeding investment, a Taipei newspaper reported on Sunday.

The project in northern Australia would focus on shrimp breeding and processing, the Commercial Times quoted Yang Tsong-tze, chairman of the party's Central Investment Holding Co Ltd, as saying State-owned Taiwan Sugar Company had promised to provide technical assistance in the project in a bid to help more Taiwanese aquatic breeders to move their operations to northern Australia, Yang was quoted as saying.
Yang said work on the project would start soon but did not give details such as the amount of the investment.

In May, the party's Asia Pacific Holding Co said it was considering an investment project in Australia, including a 1,400-km railway construction from Darwin to Alice Springs and other investments along the railway.
The Nationalist Party is one of the world's richest political parties, with net assets in seven holding companies totalling more than T$37.8 billion.
